validation.raw_csv: All summarized metric values and units match raw CSV exactly. One target kernel row present.
validation.metadata: Report metadata equals setup.json. Counts satisfy source classifier identities below; raw captured routing tensors were not saved, so this review does not independently regenerate the 191 valid rows from tensor bytes.
validation.correctness: Reported official full-expert reference passes; isolated-down exact repeat before/after profiling passes. Different from proving all-shape correctness.

read_bytes.check: exact equality to raw DRAM bytes

write_bytes.check: exact equality to raw DRAM bytes

routing_counts.implication: 91.48% of launched CTAs return before the expensive K loop. This is not 91.48% of elapsed time. Of 3328 K-loop CTAs, 30.77% are padding-only. Useful groups still have only191/288=66.32% valid rows.

measured_counters.scope: Cold-cache kernel replay observations, including early-return and padding work. Active-warp and elapsed tensor metrics use different denominators. Profiler latency is excluded from performance claims.

inference.supported_hypothesis: High long-scoreboard stalls with substantial active warps but few eligible warps and very low tensor activity prioritize the operand-loading/dependency chain and serialized K16 feeding. This is stronger evidence than a generic low-occupancy diagnosis.
not_proven: DRAM bytes alone neither prove bad coalescing nor exclude HBM saturation; this minimal metric set does not measure sustained DRAM bandwidth directly.
Long-scoreboard identifies L1TEX dependency waits, potentially global/local loads; it does not identify which operand or distinguish issue pressure, cache misses and latency without further evidence.
Low CTA-barrier stall share does not prove the immediate WGMMA wait or serial pipeline is cheap; these dependencies need not appear in the CTA-barrier category.
Rejected CTA count does not establish scheduling-only speedup, and aggregate occupancy includes different CTA lifetimes.
One routing fixture is not representative proof across M8/M32/M128/M256 or all skew patterns.

source_level_facts_not_instruction_measu.per_nonreturning_CTA: 256 K16 iterations; each contains three CTA barrier statements, shared-operand fence, weight/scale decode, one WGMMA issue, commit and immediate wait_group0.
source_level_facts_not_instruction_measu.source_expressions: 262144 packed-byte references versus131072 distinct packed bytes;262144 scale references versus16384 distinct scale bytes. Compiler/CSE, warp transactions and caches determine actual instructions and traffic.
source_level_facts_not_instruction_measu.investigation: Inspect SASS load width/address mapping plus L1TEX load requests/sectors and L2 hit/sector metrics before attributing the long-scoreboard share to poor coalescing. Preserve same kernel hash and separate profiler from clean timings.

prioritized_queue.candidate: Cheap exact all-padding subgroup early exit and filtered task scheduling
prioritized_queue.why: Eliminate demonstrably unnecessary full K-loop work and reduce empty launch dispatch with small mathematical change
prioritized_queue.guard: Every CTA uniformly checks all8 slot indices; never reject partially valid group; output zeroing and empty-local graph semantics preserved
prioritized_queue.model: If expensive CTA costs were equal and dominated runtime, dropping16/52 all-padding groups alone yields52/36=1.444x downkernel. This is not a measured bound or a forecast for full serving.
prioritized_queue.validation: Frozen correctness including partial/padding/empty groups, then paired actual expert timing

prioritized_queue.candidate: Bounded persistent-grid cap sweep after identical-math correctness
prioritized_queue.why: Isolate launch-overhead reduction from loss of latency hiding
prioritized_queue.risk: At balanced mapping2CTAs/SM supplies only8warps versus observed33.75 and measured9CTA/36warp register ceiling. An8SM grid supplies at most32warps;16SM leaves enough work for the9CTA residency limit. Do not equate grid cap with actual occupancy.
prioritized_queue.validation: Same scheduling implementation and source math across caps; balanced paired timings on at least M8/M128/M256, keep pristine v1 as development control; no heldout gate changes

prioritized_queue.candidate: Packed operand layout/load reuse and K64 software pipeline
prioritized_queue.why: Targets the observed operand dependency bottleneck rather than only wasted dispatch
prioritized_queue.bounded_first_step: Audit actual SASS and address map; implement lossless load-time packed permutation or vectorized FP4/group-scale loads as a separate variant before combining with overlap
prioritized_queue.invariants: No BF16-expanded weight bank; preserve dequant rounding and FP32 accumulation/global-scale output order; retain official oracle tolerances
prioritized_queue.estimate: No defensible numeric gain yet; most plausible route to major v1 recovery, but v1 is far slower than incumbent and recovery is not incumbent improvement.

objective_alignment: WGMMA v1 down replacement regresses full expert heavily. Prioritize bounded experiments and reject unless they recover incumbent performance; neither counters nor scheduler cleanup support a3x serving claim. Full serving impact remains unknown.
